key_concepts: Animals can be grouped into mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, and amphibians.
Each of the six animal groups has distinguishing characteristics.
Animals can be classified as vertebrates or invertebrates.
Animals can be warm-blooded or cold-blooded.
Some animal groups have jointed legs while others have no legs.
Biological classification helps organize and understand living things.
Not all fungi are harmful to humans.
Mushrooms, yeast, and molds are types of fungi.
Fungi help decompose dead plants and animals.
Bacteria are found in many places, not only dirty places.
Bacteria are not always harmful; some are used to make medicines.
Bacteria are microscopic and cannot be seen with the naked eye.
